Signals.description:
Validated telemetry snapshot from the iOS app.

All 17 phone fields are required; extra fields are forbidden.
``device_ts`` must carry timezone information (naive datetimes are rejected
by the ``_reject_naive_device_ts`` validator so that the scoring engine
never silently misclassifies a tick).

Reused by the T1.6 telemetry endpoint as the request body type.

Bounds (enforced by Pydantic):
- ``steps_10m``, ``steps_since_window`` ∈ [0, 5000]
- ``walking_sec_10m``, ``stationary_sec_10m`` ∈ [0, 600]
- ``battery_level`` ∈ [0.0, 1.0] or ``None``
- ``seq`` ≥ 0
Signals.title: Signals

WakeRules.description:
Complete wake-engine rules document.

``version`` is the schema/document version (integer, monotonically
increasing in the DB).  It is **not** the DB ``RuleVersion.version``
column — that is assigned by :func:`activate_new_version`.
WakeRules.title: WakeRules

WakeRulesWindow.description:
Window section of ``wake_rules.yaml``.

Parses the nested ``weekday: {start, end}`` / ``weekend: {start, end}``
shape from the YAML file and exposes :meth:`to_window_config` for the
scoring engine.

``holidays_as_weekend`` is a list of ISO-8601 date strings (e.g.
``"2026-12-25"``); invalid dates raise a ``ValueError``.
WakeRulesWindow.title: WakeRulesWindow

put.description:
Validate and activate a new WakeRules document.

Raw request bytes are read so that both the Content-Length pre-check AND
an actual ``len(raw) > _MAX_BODY_BYTES`` guard cover chunked transfers
where ``Content-Length`` is absent.  The bytes are decoded with
``json.loads`` before Pydantic validation so that malformed JSON surfaces
as ``422 rules_invalid`` rather than a bare 400.
Requests exceeding ``_MAX_BODY_BYTES`` are rejected with **413**.

Returns:
    ``200`` — SHA matches active version (no-op).
    ``201`` — New version created.

Raises:
    :class:`~chronos.errors.ProblemException` 422 ``rules_invalid`` with
        ``errors: [{loc, msg, type}]`` on validation failure.

post.description:
Pair a new device.

The pairing code is validated against the most recently generated active
code (non-consumed, tracked by attempt count).  A correct code issues a
fresh bearer token; an incorrect code increments the attempt counter and
burns the code after 5 failures.

Returns:
    201 with :class:`PairResponse`.

Raises:
    :class:`~chronos.errors.ProblemException` 409 if an active device exists.
    :class:`~chronos.errors.ProblemException` 400 for invalid/burned codes.
    :class:`~chronos.errors.ProblemException` 410 for expired codes.
    :class:`~chronos.errors.ProblemException` 429 when rate-limited.
